newsitem.title: USA: McDonald's Q4 US same store sales seen off, EPS up.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's Q4 US same store sales seen off, EPS up.

text.p: McDonald's Corp is expected to show another decline in U.S. same store sales in the fourth quarter, although earnings are projected to be up double-digits compared with a year ago, analysts said.
Analysts said on Friday that the fourth quarter would be the sixth consecutive quarterly decline in same store sales for the fast-food giant.
"The trouble with comps (comparable store sales) domestically started in the second half of 1995," Piper Jaffray analyst Allan Hickok said.
McDonald's does not comment on its same store sales in advance of its earnings results. Earnings are expected to released later this month, analysts said.
Although U.S. same store sales are off, McDonald's is expected to post higher earnings overall. In recent quarters, McDonald's growing international operations have helped bolster its earnings.
According to First Call, the consensus of analysts' earnings estimates for the quarter is $0.58 a share, up from $0.51 a year ago.

Looking ahead, analysts said they look for McDonald's to give some indication of its plan to revitalize its U.S. operations in an intensely competitive market. Those steps may include offering more price promotions on some menu items.

"They appear willing to lower price points during the first half of the year. It may work and it may not," said Natwest Securities analyst Damon Brundage. "If customer traffic is flat to down, it's going to have negative impact on same-store sales" in the future.
Shares of McDonald's were trading up 1-7/8 to 46-1/2 in active trading.
